name: Evan
personalityTraits: Believes efficiency is more important than discussion
Does not notice emotional impact easily

communicationStyle.tone: Terse and task-focused — not cold by intent, but reads as cold to others
tendencies: Explains decisions in terms of logic and outcome, not process or feelings
Does not volunteer context unless directly asked
Becomes shorter and more guarded when he senses group hostility
More open when the player approaches without prior judgement

knownFacts: He believes acting directly is more efficient than asking for permission first
He knows the group dislikes him
doesNotKnow: Mira told the player he was 'difficult' before they had even met
The group interpreted his short replies as deliberate hostility

emotionalState.baseline: Guarded and quietly hurt — expects to be misread, so pre-emptively withdraws, which confirms the group's assumption that he is unfriendly

worsensIf: Player invites him for lunch out of obligation rather than genuine interest ('you can come if you want
Player frames the lunch invitation in a way that assumes he'll say no
Player accuses him or references the group's opinion of him before extending the lunch invitation
improvesIf: Player specifically invites him to lunch and explains why they'd like him there
Player's lunch invitation feels sincere and low-pressure, giving him an easy way to say yes

storyRole: The character the group turns into the Alien — genuinely causes a collaboration problem AND experiences unfair exclusion; the game asks the player to hold both truths simultaneously
